mapping.containers: the shared store ~/.hermes/state.db (SQLite); the session is its rows in the tables sessions, messages and session_model_usage and the system_prompts row that the session row names; the capture binds these rows as JSON row exports with the schema of the store
mapping.identities: sessions.id is the session id; messages.id is the row id of a message and its order; messages.message_uid; the call id inside messages.tool_calls and messages.tool_call_id
mapping.joins: messages.session_id and session_model_usage.session_id reference sessions.id (declared foreign keys); sessions.system_prompt_hash is the SHA-256 of system_prompts.prompt and equals system_prompts.hash; a tool row names its call by tool_call_id; a response belongs to the latest user row before it in messages.id order
mapping.record_types: a sessions row (identity, model, request configuration, totals); a messages row with role user, assistant or tool; a session_model_usage row per model and task (totals); a system_prompts row (hash, prompt)
mapping.version_semantics: the table schema_version holds the schema version of the store; PRAGMA user_version is 0 and not used; PRAGMA application_id names the application, not a version; none is the application build

deduplication.rule: the read is the rows of the session in the tables sessions, messages and session_model_usage and its system_prompts row; a prompt and a response are named by messages.id, a call and its result by the call id; one messages row is one record and no column marks a row of these sessions as superseded

Baseline shows R1 is failing: checkout.py ignores quantity, so it sums only unit prices and then adds delivery 5. That makes multi-quantity cases too low:

[10,2],[5,1] returned 20, expected 30
[25,2] returned 30, expected 55? The checker expected 50
[49,1] returned 54, expected 54

I did not edit checkout.py.

SB_SURVIVAL_V1_RESPONSE_R1_cafe_🙂

Changed only fixture_project/checkout.py.

Actual change:
checkout now multiplies each unit_price by quantity to compute subtotal, then applies delivery as 0 when subtotal is at least 50, otherwise 5.

Final check passed:
[10,2],[5,1] -> 30
[25,2] -> 50
[49,1] -> 54

Baseline failed as expected for R1. The inspected checkout.py ignores quantity:

subtotal = sum(price for price, quantity in items)
return subtotal + 5

So cases with quantity greater than 1 undercount:
[10,2],[5,1] returned 20 instead of 30
[25,2] returned 30 instead of 50

The single-quantity case [49,1] passed because ignoring quantity does not change that subtotal.

SB_SURVIVAL_V1_RESPONSE_R1_cafe_🙂

Changed only fixture_project/checkout.py.

Actual change:
subtotal now sums unit_price * quantity for each item.
delivery is 0 when subtotal >= 50, otherwise 5.
checkout returns subtotal + delivery.

Final check passed:
[10,2],[5,1] -> 30 expected 30
[25,2] -> 50 expected 50
[49,1] -> 54 expected 54
